why: The ORDER is the feature: pre-shutdown callbacks run while the session is still open and every entity still works -- which is how a device publishes a final state, answers a last request, parks an actuator or releases a bus -- and on-shutdown callbacks run after the close. rclrs has no shutdown hook at all -- no `Context` callback list, no free function -- so there is nothing on the rclrs side to correspond to. It exists because an RTOS node has nowhere else to release hardware while its entities still work. The platform constraint is no allocator: rclcpp's registration takes a `std::function<void()>` (a heap allocation per callback) and hands back a handle owning a `std::shared_ptr` to it. Ours is a fixed-capacity static table of `(extern "C" fn, void* context)` sized by `NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS` (default 2, small on issue 0460's precedent that a per-entity static slot is a cost every image pays), and the handle is the SLOT INDEX with its phase packed in so it cannot remove the other phase's callback. rclcpp hangs these on `Context`; we have none (see `c:context_*` / `cpp:Context` in init/), and the executor is what `shutdown` / `close` / `fini` is called on, so it owns the tables. Issue 0790.
